C.S vs Bhagyamma on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67431438/

1 Petitioner asserting to be an injured suffered in a RTA filed petition under Section 166 of M.V.Act claiming compensation from the respondents who are the owner and insurer of the Motorcycle bearing No.KA-52-U-5675 asserting that on 25.01.2023 at about 17.30 p.m. when standing on the footpath to cross the road at Bhudihal gate, Bhudhihal - Mandigere road, Nelamangala Taluk,
Bengaluru, rider of Motorcycle bearing No.KA-52-U-5675, rode the same negligently from Bhudihal towards Bhudhihal gate, dashed the same to the petitioner, thereby caused accident, caused injuries to the petitioner.
2. Petitioner took treatment at J.P.hospital, Nelamangala and as on the date of accident petitioner being aged about 29 years, used to earn Rs.25,000/p.m. by working as Tailor.

3. Regarding accident Nelamangala Rural police registered crime No.11/2023 against the rider of the Motorcycle bearing No.KA-52-U-5675.
4.
In spite of service of notice, respondent No.1 - owner of the motorcycle remained absent.

5. In response to the notice, respondent No.2- insurance company appeared through his Advocate,
filed written statement, denying the allegation regarding reason, mode of accident, age, occupation,
income, nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioner.

6. On the basis of the pleadings on 21.08.2024, this Authority has framed the following issues :
1. Whether the Petitioner proves that on 25.01.2023 at about 17.30 hours, beside Bhudihala Mandigere road, near Bhudihala gate, Nelamangala village, Taluk,
Benglauru Rural District, in view of the negligent use of the motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-52-U-5675 accident taken place resulting in the injuries to the petitioner ?
2.
Whether the Petitioner is entitled to compensation ?
If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order ?
7. On 22.04.2024, 27.09.2024 petitioner deposed as PW1 and produced 13 documents at Ex.P.1 to P.13.

On 25.06.2024, 29.10.2024 petitioner produced the evidence of Dr. Nagaraj B.N. as PW2 and get produced 2 documents at Ex.P.14 and P.15.
8.
I heard the arguments submitted on behalf of both contesting parties and perused the records.

9. On the basis of the record, my findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1 ...
In the affirmative Issue No.2 ...

Petitioner is entitle to receive Rs.3,71,182/-
with current and future interest at 6% p.a. as compensation from the respondents.

Shilpa.C.S vs Bhagyamma on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67431438/
2 Issue No.3 ...

As per final order for the following:-
REASONS 10. Issue No.1 :- In the evidence petitioner stated that on 25.01.2023 at about 17.30 p.m. when standing on the footpath to cross the road at Bhudihal gate, Bhudihal - Mandigere road,
Nelamangala Taluk, Bengaluru, rider of Motorcycle bearing No.KA-52-U-5675, rode the same negligently from Bhudihal towards Bhudhihal gate, dashed the same to the petitioner, thereby caused accident, caused injuries to the petitioner.
11.
In the written statement respondent No.2- insurance company denied the allegation regarding reason and mode of the accident.

12. In the cross-examination petitioner/PW.1 denied the suggestion that when sitting on the pillion of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-52-H-8805 rode by her husband fell along with the motorcycle,
suffered injuries.
Petitioner denied the suggestion that motorcycle bearing No.KA-52- H-8805 neither dashed to her nor concerned to the injuries might have been suffered.
During recording of evidence of PW.1 husband of the petitioner who is in the court hall shown his Driving Licence No.KA06 2014000000385 dated 30.12.2013.
13. In the evidence PW.2- Dr. Nagaraj B.N. stated nothing regarding reason and mode of the accident.

14. Ex.P.1 is the copy of the FIR with complaint pertaining to crime No.11/2023 registered by Nelamangala Rural police against rider of Motorcycle bearing No.KA-52- U-5675 for having committed offence punishable under Section 279,337 of IPC, Sec.187 of MV Act regarding the accident taken place on 25.01.2023 at 5.30 p.m. resulting in the injuries to the petitioner, on the basis of the statement of petitioner recorded in the hospital.
Ex.P.2 is the crime detail form.
Ex.P.3 is the motor vehicle seizure mahazar.
Ex.P.4 is the IMV Report.
Ex.P.5 is the wound certificate in which reason for the injuries is noted as alleged RTA on 25.01.2023 at 5.30 p.m..

Ex.P.6 is the copy of the charge sheet filed by Nelamangala Rural Police in crime No.11/2023 against Manu M. S/o Mahadeva rider of Motorcycle bearing No.KA-52-U-5675 for having committed offence punishable under Section 279, 338 of IPC and Sec.187 of MV Act.
15.
In this case respondents have not produced any type of evidence to disbelieve the evidence placed by the petitioner regarding reason, mode and consequence of accident.

Hence, I have concluded that on 25.01.2023 at about 17.30 p.m. when petitioner was standing on the footpath to cross the road at Bhudihal gate, Bhudihal - Mandigere road, Nelamangala Taluk, Bengaluru, Manu M. S/o Mahadeva- rider of Motorcycle bearing No.KA-52-U- 5675, rode the same negligently from Bhudihal towards Bhudhihal gate, dashed the same to the petitioner, thereby caused accident,
caused injuries to the petitioner.
Hence, I answer issue No.1 in the affirmative.

16. Issue No.2: In the evidence petitioner stated that in the accident she has suffered injuries to face i.e., facial bone fracture, right maxilla (anterior wall) orbital floor, interior orbital floor, interior
Shilpa

. C.S vs Bhagyamma on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67431438/
3 orbital margin fracture and zygomatic arch, right little finger MP x anterior dislocation at PIP joint with Zone 3 extensor tendon injury, took treatment at J.P. hospital, Nelamangala, as inpatient from 25.01.2023 to 30.01.2023 by spending Rs.2,00,000/-, as on the date of accident used to earn Rs.25,000/-p.m. by working as Tailor.
17.
In the written statement, respondent No.2- insurance company denied the allegation regarding nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioner.
18. In the cross-examination, petitioner denied the suggestion that in the alleged accident she neither suffered grievous injuries nor underwent surgery nor spent Rs.2,00,000/- for treatment.
Petitioner admitted that bill produced at Sl. No.9 worth Rs.5,000/- is advance bill.
Petitioner denied suggestion about the fabrication of the bill for the purpose of the case.

19. In the evidence affidavit PW.2 Dr. Nagaraju B.N., Orthopedic Surgeon at Sai Ortho and Dental Center stated that on 01.06.2024 when clinically examined the petitioner noticed that petitioner suffered permanent physical disability at 27% to hand which is about 9% to the whole body.
In the evidence PW.2 produced OPD card and X-ray at Ex.P.14 and P.15.

In the cross-examination PW.2 admitted that he neither treated the petitioner, nor verified inpatient/followup treatment record of the petitioner nor collected opinion of the doctor who treated the petitioner.
PW.2 stated that as on 01.06.2024 fractures of the petitioner are united and Metacarpal fracture of the petitioner has been treated conservatively.
In this case petitioner has not produced any documentary evidence regarding quantum of the income.

20. Wound certificate, discharge summary, prescriptions, medical bills, X-ray and other medical records shows that in the accident petitioner suffered swelling over right side of the face, step deformity at infra orbital margin, depressed fracture of right zygomatic arch, anterior dislocation of right PIP joint of little finger, abrasions over dorsum of right hand and right forearm, facial bone fractures, right maxilla (anterior wall), took treatment at J.P. Hospital, Nelamangala as inpatient from 26.01.2023 to 30.01.2023.
21.
In the Aadhaar card marked at Ex.P.8 the date birth of the petitioner is noted as 24.05.1993.
The medical bills shows that the petitioner spent approximately Rs.1,06,182/- for treatment.
The bill produced at serial No.9 marked at Ex.P.9 is with respect to implant charges worth Rs.5,000/-.

In the file there are no documents regarding either decrease in the income of the petitioner or loss of income of the petitioner subsequent to the treatment taken for the injuries suffered in the accident.

Hence, I have inferred that the oral evidence of PW.2 Dr.Nagaraj B.N. is not sufficient to award compensation under the head loss of future income(Permanent Physical Disability).
22.

Considering the nature of injuries suffered by the petitioner, length, place and nature of treatment taken by the petitioner, lack of documents regarding quantum of the petitioner regarding Rs.5,000/- spent towards implants as noted in the bills produced at Sl.No.9, I award Rs.1,00,000/-
towards pain and suffering, Rs.1,06,182/- towards medical expenses, Rs.10,000/- towards attendant, conveyance and nourishment charges, Rs.80,000/- (Rs.16,000 x 5) towards loss of income during treatment period and Rs.75,000/- towards loss of amenities and future happiness.

4
Hence, I come to the conclusion that the petitioner is entitle to receive compensation at Rs.3,71,182/- with current and future interest at 6% per annum.
23. Hence, I came to the conclusion that the petitioner is entitle for Rs.3,71,182/- with current and future interest at the rate of 6% p.a. as compensation.
Sl . No
. Head of Compensation Amount/Rs 1. Pain and sufferings 1,00,000-00 2.
Medical expenses 1,06,182-00 3.
Attendant conveyance and 10,000-00 nourishment charges 4. Loss of income during 80,000-00 treatment period 5. Loss of amenities and future 75,000-00 unhappiness
In the written statement, respondent No.2- insurance company admitted subsistence of policy with respect to Motorcycle bearing No.KA-52-U-5675 as on the date of accident.
In the file there are no evidence to show that as on the date of accident respondent No.1-owner of the motorcycle violated any terms of the policy.

Hence, I came to the conclusion that the respondents being the insurer and owner of the Motorcycle bearing No.KA-52-U- 5675 are liable to pay compensation and an award is to be passed directing the respondents to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, I answer issue No.2 accordingly and pass the following :
ORDER The petition filed under Section 166 of IMV Act is partly allowed.

The respondents shall either jointly or severally pay Rs.3,71,182/- (Rupees three lakhs seventy one thousand one hundred eighty two only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from 31.07.2023, to petitioner towards compensation.
The respondent No.2, being the Insurer of the Motorcycle bearing No.KA-52-U-5675 shall deposit the compensation amount with interest within 3 months from today.
After deposit of the compensation amount, entire compensation amount and interest may be released to the petitioner by crediting the same to her bank account directly.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/- .
Draw an Award accordingly.

(Dictated to the Stenographer, transcribed by her, corrected, signed and then pronounced by me in the Open Court on this the 6th day of February, 2025)
(J.N.SUBRAMANYA) Chief Judge, Court of Small Causes & Member, Prl. M.A.C.T.
Bangalore.
